summary: The Iran war's oil shock is stoking inflation fears and bond market pressure, with concerns the Fed may be behind the curve — while the three-day Trump-Xi Beijing summit closed without a meaningful breakthrough on the Strait of Hormuz standoff. US 10-year yields posted their biggest weekly jump since Trump's tariffs roiled markets in April 2025, hammering bonds and gold while leaving equities holding gains on trade truce optimism.
tweet: Oil above $105 and a Trump-Xi summit that delivered no Iran breakthrough sent global bond yields to multi-year highs this week, splitting stocks from bonds and gold.
